title: Residential Electricity Supply: Agreements per Customer and per Premise
content:
**Rule.** A residential customer may hold several Beacon Ridge electricity agreements under Residential Electricity Supply, one per premise, up to 4 agreements at the same time. An agreement counts toward that limit while its status is enrollment pending, active or drop pending; closed, rescinded and rejected agreements do not count. When the limit is reached the enrollment is refused.

**One live agreement per premise.** No other Residential Electricity Supply agreement on the same premise may be in enrollment pending, active or drop pending status when a new enrollment is submitted. A premise can be supplied by only one supplier per commodity, so a second enrollment on a premise that already has a live Beacon Ridge electricity agreement is refused and the customer is offered a plan change on the existing agreement instead.

**Basis of judgement.** Both tests are read from the company's agreement records, as they stand before the enrollment is submitted: the per-premise test looks at the agreements recorded against the premise being enrolled, and the count toward the limit looks at the statuses of the customer's agreements. A customer's own account of what they hold does not replace those records.

| Status of an existing agreement | Counts toward the limit of 4 | Blocks a new enrollment on the same premise |
|---|---|---|
| enrollment pending | yes | yes |
| active | yes | yes |
| drop pending | yes | yes |
| closed | no | no |
| rescinded | no | no |
| rejected | no | no |

**Illustrations (hypothetical customers).**

- A customer holds three active agreements at three addresses and asks to enroll a fourth address with no Beacon Ridge electricity agreement on it. Three agreements count, the fourth would make 4, which is within the limit; the per-premise test is met.
- A customer holds four agreements, one of them drop pending. All four count, so a fifth enrollment is refused.
- A customer whose agreement at an address is closed after a switch-away asks to enroll that same address again. The closed agreement neither counts nor blocks the premise.
- A customer asks to enroll an address whose agreement is still active. The enrollment is refused and a plan change on the existing agreement is offered instead.
